name: Settings
description: A layout for preferences as rows, with a label and a short hint on one side and the control on the other, grouped under headings. A row can also link to a sub-page or run an action like signing out.

classes.ayy-settings: A group: <section aria-labelledby> holding a title, an optional description and the list. Groups after each other get space between them.
classes.ayy-settings--plain: No card around the rows (inside a dialog, a sheet, or a page already on a surface); rows lose their inline padding.
classes.ayy-settings__title: The group's heading, an <h2> ("Notifications") that labels the section.
classes.ayy-settings__description: A muted line under the heading.
classes.ayy-settings__list: The rows, in a card with a line border; hairlines between rows.
classes.ayy-settings__row: One setting: text at the start, the control at the end. Wraps the control under the text when there isn't room (a phone).
classes.ayy-settings__row--stack: The control under the text at full width: a textarea, a radio list, a group of choice cards. The row doesn't wrap.
classes.ayy-settings__label: The setting's name: a <label for> pointing at the control, or a <span> when the control is labelled otherwise.
classes.ayy-settings__hint: One muted line explaining the setting; give it an id and point the control's aria-describedby at it. With ayy-field__error it's an error.
classes.ayy-settings__control: The control's box at the end of the row. Inputs and selects in it get a sensible minimum width.
classes.ayy-settings__link: On an .ayy-settings__row that is an <a href> (opens a sub-page) or a <button> (runs an action): the whole row is the target, with a chevron icon at the end.
classes.ayy-settings__value: The current value in a link row, muted, before the chevron ("English", "System").
classes.ayy-settings__link--destructive: Sign out, Delete account: red text and no chevron.
classes.ayy-settings__picker: A grid of larger pictures to choose from in a stacked row (an appearance setting that should show every choice at once): role="radiogroup" with an aria-label. For a dropdown, use a Select with pictures.
classes.ayy-settings__option: One picture to choose: a <label> around a visually hidden native radio, a .ayy-settings__preview and a .ayy-settings__caption. Chosen: the picture gets a text-colour border and the caption turns the text colour.
classes.ayy-settings__preview: The picture's 16:10 frame in a SettingsOption. Holds a .ayy-settings__screen, or a short sample such as "Aa" in a font. aria-hidden: the caption names the option. (In a Select, the screen goes straight in its .ayy-select__picture.)
classes.ayy-settings__caption: The option's name under the picture ("Dark", "Sharp").
classes.ayy-settings__screen: A miniature app (sidebar, heading, lines, a primary button) drawn from the tokens around it, for Theme, Corners and Text direction: in a Select's pictures (.ayy-select__picture) or a SettingsOption's. Set data-theme, data-density or dir on it, or brand and corner tokens on or around it, to preview them; it mirrors in RTL. Two in one picture split it, the second showing the right half: System as light then dark, Auto density as compact then touch, Auto direction as dir="ltr" then dir="rtl".
classes.ayy-settings__screen--rows: For Density: a list of rows, each a line of text and a control, divided by hairlines; rows are as tall as data-density makes them (exaggerated), so Compact shows about two and a half times the rows Touch does.
classes.ayy-settings__screen--brand: For Brand colour: where the primary colour shows (the chosen sidebar item tinted, a filled progress bar, a ticked checkbox, the primary button). Set --ayy-color-primary on it to preview a colour (a palette token; var(--ayy-color-text) for the monochrome default).

default.looks: A semibold heading and a muted description over a bordered card of rows split by hairlines: a medium label and a small muted hint at the start, the control at the end.

hover.looks: A wash over the link row; an option's picture gets the line-hover border.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a link row opens its page at once.

focus.looks: Link rows get the ring inside the row's edge (outside in plain groups); an option's picture gets the ring 2px outside; controls keep their own ring.

disabled.looks: Reduced opacity and not-allowed cursor on link rows and options.

selected.looks: The picture gets a text-colour border plus a 1px ring, and the caption turns the text colour. Forced colours: a Highlight outline. Rows themselves aren't selectable: a link row shows its current value (.ayy-settings__value).

error.looks: The hint becomes the error, in the destructive colour.

loading.none: Settings apply at once. While they load, show a Skeleton in the shape of the rows.

destructive.looks: Sign out, delete the account: red label, no chevron.

sizes.density: Rows are at least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch); their controls follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. A row wraps its control under the label when there's no room; stack does it always. Inputs and popover triggers in a row are at least 11rem, selects 12.5rem (room for a picture). A picker is a grid of 8.5rem-minimum columns with 16:10 pictures. A screen's parts are sized in container units of its picture, so one drawing fits a grid tile and both of a Select's pictures.

js: settingsClass({ plain?, className? }), settingsRowClass({ stack?, link?, destructive?, className? }) → class strings; settingsChevronIcon (SVG markup for a link row's chevron, mirrored in RTL); settingsPickerClass, settingsOptionClass, settingsPreviewClass, settingsCaptionClass, settingsScreenClass constants; settingsScreenVariants ("app", "rows", "brand": add ayy-settings__screen--rows or --brand). A custom colour Select: settingsColorInput(select) finds the hidden <input type="color" data-value> right after its wrapper, openSettingsColor(select) opens ayywi's colour picker under the select when that option is chosen (call it on change and on ayy-choose, after the list closes), syncSettingsColor(input) shows the colour in that option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements does all three page-wide. Apply the picks with setTheme(), setDensity() and setBrand(); data-motion="reduce" and dir for motion and direction.

react.import: import { Settings, SettingsRow, SettingsLink, SettingsPicker, SettingsOption, SettingsScreen } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.title: ReactNode — the heading; the section is labelled by it
props.description: ReactNode — a line under the heading
props.plain: boolean — no card around the rows

props.label: ReactNode — the setting's name
props.htmlFor: string — the control's id: the label becomes a <label for>, and the hint gets the id `${htmlFor}-hint` for the control's aria-describedby
props.error: ReactNode — replaces the hint, in red, with role="alert"
props.stack: boolean — the control under the text at full width

SettingsLink.renders: <a class="ayy-settings__row ayy-settings__link" href> with href, else <button type="button">; a directional chevron unless destructive

props.label: ReactNode — what it opens or does
props.hint: ReactNode — a line under the label
props.value: ReactNode — the current value, before the chevron
props.href: string — opens a page: the row is an <a>; without it a <button>
props.type / disabled: Button rows only. type defaults to "button"

props.name: string — shared radio name; generated if omitted

props.label: ReactNode — the caption, which names the radio
props.preview: ReactNode — the picture; a SettingsScreen by default, or a sample like "Aa" in a font or at a text size

SettingsScreen.renders: <span class="ayy-settings__screen" data-theme data-density aria-hidden="true">; two of them for theme="system" (light, dark) or density="auto" (compact, touch)

props.variant: "app" | "rows" | "brand" — what it draws: the app (Theme, Corners, Text direction), rows (Density) or the primary colour's places (Brand colour; set --ayy-color-primary in style)
props.theme: "system" | "light" | "dark" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" — the theme it's drawn in; omit for the one around it
props.density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" | "auto" — the density it's drawn in; omit for the one around it

a11y: Each group is a <section> labelled by its <h2>, so screen-reader users can jump between groups.
Every control needs a name: give SettingsRow htmlFor and the control that id, so the label is a real <label for>. For a Switch, put the id on the switch's input.
Point the control's aria-describedby at the hint (`${htmlFor}-hint`) so the explanation is read with it.
A link row is one <a> or <button>: its whole text, value included, is its name. Use <a href> when it opens a page, <button> when it does something.
Controls wrap under the label on narrow screens instead of shrinking below a usable size.
A picker is a radiogroup of native radios: arrow keys move between options, and each option is named by its caption. The pictures are aria-hidden.

A custom colour's <input type="color"> is hidden and out of the tab order: choosing Custom opens the colour picker as a labelled dialog under the select with focus in it, and Esc or Enter closes it and puts focus back on the select.
do: Use it for any settings or preferences screen: group related rows under short headings (General, Notifications, Shortcuts). They open in a near-full-screen Dialog (size="full") holding the App shell in settings mode (the Settings pattern): a sidebar of sections and one section's groups in the main.
Keep labels short and put the why in the hint ("Show a badge with the number of tasks due today").
Use a Switch for on/off that applies at once, a Select for one of several, a Shortcut recorder for key bindings.
On phones, use link rows with the current value for anything with more than a few choices, and open a sub-page.
Put Sign out or Delete account last, in its own group, as a destructive link row.

For appearance settings, use the same controls in every product: Theme, Density, Text size, Brand colour, Corners, Font and Text direction each as a Select with pictures: SettingsScreens for Theme, Corners and Text direction (dir on the screen), variant="rows" for Density, variant="brand" with --ayy-color-primary for Brand colour (its last option, Custom, opens the colour picker on a hidden <input type="color" data-value="custom"> after the select), and "Aa" samples for Font and Text size. Use Surface colour and Contrast Sliders with setThemeCustomization(), passing the active brand colour. Reduce motion as a Switch, Language as a Select, and Reset appearance as a destructive link row. Apply each at once with setTheme(), setDensity(), setBrand(), data-motion and dir.
dont: Don't add a Save button for switches and selects that apply at once; save as they change and confirm with a Toast if needed.
Don't put two controls in one row; split the setting.
Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies at once — that's what a Switch says.
Don't nest a card inside the list; use another group.

Don't draw your own theme thumbnails, or use a Select without pictures or a button opening a popover for Theme, Density, Text size, Brand colour, Corners, Font or Text direction: a Select whose pictures are SettingsScreens draws each choice from its real tokens.
Don't open settings in a small or side Dialog, or switch sections with Tabs; use a size="full" Dialog with the App shell's settings mode. --plain is for a sheet with a couple of quick options.
